name: Ballpit-TS-TW
title: Ballpit
description: A 3D physics toy of dozens of glossy spheres in white, grey and graphite that fall, collide and settle into a heap on a black stage. Moving the cursor pushes them around.
use: You want a playful, physics-driven 3D backdrop for a hero or landing page that responds to the pointer.
avoid: It is a continuous simulation with hundreds of collision checks per frame, heavy on low-end phones.
a11y: The physics keeps moving forever and ignores reduced-motion; the canvas has no label or pause control. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A black stage holds a heap of glossy 3D spheres in white, light grey and dark graphite, of mixed sizes, piled along the bottom and drifting upward. A bright white glow forms in the middle of the pile, and a white 'Ballpit' heading with a small grey subtitle floats near the top.
behaves: Gravity pulls the spheres down so they bounce off the floor and walls and shove each other, then settle into a loose heap. Moving the cursor drags an invisible control sphere that knocks them around before they calm again.
customise: Props pass count, colours, gravity, friction, wall bounce, sphere sizes, material and light settings, plus the follow-cursor toggle. The demo heading and subtitle are separate page markup.
weight: heavy: 140 spheres with pairwise collision checks and a Three.js render loop on every frame.
